Which of the five colleges had the highest total admissions over the 5 years?

The table shows MBA admissions in five colleges A to E over five years.

| College \ Year | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 140 | 135 | 150 | 140 | 160 |
| B | 180 | 170 | 190 | 210 | 200 |
| C | 120 | 100 | 110 | 125 | 140 |
| D | 200 | 210 | 205 | 220 | 230 |
| E | 150 | 145 | 160 | 155 | 170 |

Out of all admissions in the year 2024, the percentage of admissions in college B is
questions.explanation:
Total admissions in 2024 $= 160 + 200 + 140 + 230 + 170 = 900$.

College B's share $= \dfrac{200}{900} \times 100 = 22.22\%$.

questions.stem:
The table shows MBA admissions in five colleges A to E over five years.

| College \ Year | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 140 | 135 | 150 | 140 | 160 |
| B | 180 | 170 | 190 | 210 | 200 |
| C | 120 | 100 | 110 | 125 | 140 |
| D | 200 | 210 | 205 | 220 | 230 |
| E | 150 | 145 | 160 | 155 | 170 |

Which college has witnessed the highest growth percentage in admissions in 2024 compared to 2020?
questions.explanation:
Growth $\% = \dfrac{2024 - 2020}{2020} \times 100$ for each college:

- A: $\dfrac{20}{140} = 14.29\%$
- B: $\dfrac{20}{180} = 11.11\%$
- **C: $\dfrac{20}{120} = 16.67\%$**
- D: $\dfrac{30}{200} = 15\%$
- E: $\dfrac{20}{150} = 13.33\%$

Four colleges gained the same 20 admissions, so the one with the **smallest 2020 base** wins — college **C**. D gained more in absolute terms (30) but on a base of 200, which is only 15%.

questions.stem:
Two pie charts show how students in colleges A and B are distributed across games. College A has **1000** students, college B has **1500**.

| Game | College A (share) | College B (sector angle) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cricket | 10% | $108^\circ$ |
| Football | 20% | $108^\circ$ |
| Boxing | 30% | $36^\circ$ |
| Tennis | 20% | $36^\circ$ |
| Chess | 20% | $72^\circ$ |

Find the total number of students who play football in both colleges A and B together.
questions.explanation:
**College A:** football is 20% of 1000 $= 200$ students.

**College B:** the football sector is $108^\circ$, so its share is $\dfrac{108}{360} = 30\%$ of 1500 $= 450$ students.

Total $= 200 + 450 = 650$.

questions.stem:
Two pie charts show how students in colleges A and B are distributed across games. College A has **1000** students, college B has **1500**.

| Game | College A (share) | College B (sector angle) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cricket | 10% | $108^\circ$ |
| Football | 20% | $108^\circ$ |
| Boxing | 30% | $36^\circ$ |
| Tennis | 20% | $36^\circ$ |
| Chess | 20% | $72^\circ$ |

With both colleges put together, which is the game played by the fewest students?
questions.explanation:
Convert both charts to head-counts (B's shares are the angle $\div\ 360$):

| Game | A (of 1000) | B (of 1500) | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cricket | 100 | 450 | 550 |
| Football | 200 | 450 | 650 |
| Boxing | 300 | 150 | 450 |
| **Tennis** | 200 | 150 | **350** |
| Chess | 200 | 300 | 500 |

**Tennis** has the smallest total. Note that boxing is the *largest* group in A, which is why the two charts must be combined rather than compared by percentage.

questions.stem:
Two pie charts show how students in colleges A and B are distributed across games. College A has **1000** students, college B has **1500**.

| Game | College A (share) | College B (sector angle) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cricket | 10% | $108^\circ$ |
| Football | 20% | $108^\circ$ |
| Boxing | 30% | $36^\circ$ |
| Tennis | 20% | $36^\circ$ |
| Chess | 20% | $72^\circ$ |

In college B, find the difference between the number of players of football and chess.
questions.explanation:
In college B, football takes $108^\circ$ and chess $72^\circ$, a gap of $36^\circ$.

Each degree is worth $\dfrac{1500}{360}$ students, so the difference $= \dfrac{36}{360} \times 1500 = 150$.

*(Longer way: football $= 450$, chess $= 300$, difference $= 150$.)*
